network.tdh.formal.metadataDescription: TDH-v1 as a Lean 4 model: what it reproduces, what its proofs establish, what turned out to be false, and what the proofs do not cover.
network.tdh.formal.title: Formal model
network.tdh.formal.lede: TDH-v1 is also written as a mathematical model in Lean 4, a language in which a computer checks every step of every proof. The model runs, so it computes real days of TDH, and it carries proofs of the rule’s key properties. This page says what is proved, what was shown false, and what the proofs do not cover.

network.tdh.formal.why.title: Why write the rule again
network.tdh.formal.why.body: Plain English can be read two ways. When a second implementation was written from the specification alone, it found 23 places where it had to guess; two were rated high, because the two readings give different results. P26 now states a rule for each.
network.tdh.formal.why.body2: A formal model leaves no such room: every term has exactly one meaning, and the computer rejects a proof with a gap. Writing it already paid off: it proved that the first version of D131’s netting rule could be changed by steps inside a transaction, in five cases, after the separately written program B found the flaw; P26’s uniform rule fixes all five, and its property is now a theorem.
network.tdh.formal.featured.title: One theorem, read two ways
network.tdh.formal.featured.plain: Take any two inputs whose transactions correspond one to one, each pair moving the same net amount of every token for every address. Replayed with netting, they leave every holding stack the same, for every token and every address. In other words: how a transaction gets to its net result, the order of its steps, round trips or detours, cannot change TDH.
network.tdh.formal.contains.title: What the model contains
network.tdh.formal.contains.body: The model covers P26 from canonical decoded inputs to the day’s records and totals, one module per part of the specification. Each definition quotes or cites its P26 section, and P26’s pseudocode sits next to the code that implements it. All arithmetic is on unbounded integers, so nothing can overflow or round by accident; the two binary64 roundings are emulated exactly.
network.tdh.formal.contains.runs: The model runs: it reproduces all 51 conformance vectors (976 checks), all 21,410 wallet and identity records of the 2026-10-11 cycle with the live total of 2,061,888,816, and 1,000 random inputs under both netting rules against the Python reference (217,200 checks). A full day takes about 6 seconds.
network.tdh.formal.contains.outside: Outside the model: selecting and decoding Ethereum logs, state reads and finality, and the binding of the result header. The vector runner has its own log decoder; it is test tooling, not part of the model.

network.tdh.formal.module.basic: Rounding, addresses, the sinks; binary64 by exact integer emulation
network.tdh.formal.module.registry: The parameter registry, its validity and its hash
network.tdh.formal.module.inputs: Decoded transfers and delegation events, canonical order (decoding itself is not modelled)
network.tdh.formal.module.cutoff: Cycle day, boundary, snapshot block, whole days
network.tdh.formal.module.eligibility: Eligibility, editions and floors, rates, seasons
network.tdh.formal.module.holdings: Acquisition stacks, the underflow test, transaction netting, the replay, per-token values
network.tdh.formal.module.arithmetic: RATE, BASE, ADD, the boost in cents, FINAL
network.tdh.formal.module.cycle: The whole cycle: records, totals, range checks, output
network.tdh.formal.statements.title: What is proved, and what is not
network.tdh.formal.statements.intro: Every theorem below is checked at every build and audited to use only Lean’s three standard axioms; a proof with a gap fails the build. Some properties are checked by running the model instead, and some claims turned out to be false.
network.tdh.formal.statements.caption: Statements, {shown} of {total} shown
network.tdh.formal.st.netting.title: Netting invariance
network.tdh.formal.st.netting.plain: Every holding stack after the replay depends only on each transaction’s net movement of each token per address. Reordering a transaction’s transfers, or inserting a round trip anywhere in it, through a sink or not, changes no stack.
network.tdh.formal.st.netting.scope: Stated for the stacks, from which balance, raw, base and final are computed, not for the output records themselves. It assumes one timestamp and txHash per transaction, which P26 §3.2 requires and the model checks. The underflow test and the edition counts still read the steps.
network.tdh.formal.st.replay.title: The replay never fails
network.tdh.formal.st.replay.plain: Once the underflow test passes, the replay succeeds, with or without netting, and every stack outside the sinks holds exactly its address’s balance: what it received minus what it sent. That is why P26 need not test for underflow again in the replay.
network.tdh.formal.st.replay.scope: A sink’s stack is not a balance: sinks only receive.
network.tdh.formal.st.conservation.title: Copies are conserved
network.tdh.formal.st.conservation.plain: Summed over every address outside the sinks, the copies held of a token are the copies that came from a sink minus those that went to one. An address that never appears holds none.
network.tdh.formal.st.conservation.scope: The inflow counts transfers from the zero address (mints) and from 0x…dead, which creates copies (P26 §3.4).
network.tdh.formal.st.totals.title: Totals
network.tdh.formal.st.totals.plain: When a day has a result, the network total is the sum of identity finals, the total without sinks leaves out exactly the zero and dead identities, the base and raw totals are sums too, and the total is below 2^53.
network.tdh.formal.st.totals.scope: A sum over wallets is a different number: see “Total = sum of wallets” below.
network.tdh.formal.st.order.title: Order independence
network.tdh.formal.st.order.plain: Reordering the input’s transfers and delegation events in any way gives the same result, or the same error. The order in which logs arrive cannot matter.
network.tdh.formal.st.order.scope: A transfer’s position fields are part of the input: changing them changes the canonical order, as it should.
network.tdh.formal.st.lifo.title: Last in, first out
network.tdh.formal.st.lifo.plain: The model’s compact stack is exactly P26’s ordered list: a purchase appends, a send removes exactly the last n entries in order and fails exactly when there are fewer, and its size is its length.
network.tdh.formal.st.lifo.scope: Seven theorems about the stack itself.
network.tdh.formal.st.facts.title: P26’s stated numbers
network.tdh.formal.st.facts.plain: The registry hash, the half-cent rate ties for H = 3,941, ADD(2) = 50,000, ADD(3) = 82,645, ADD(n) = 144,051 from 33 sets, no ties in the boost’s rounding, and the final ties that round down: 16 checks.
network.tdh.formal.st.facts.scope: Evaluated at every build, which trusts Lean’s compiler; not proved in the kernel.
network.tdh.formal.st.identitySums.title: Identity sums
network.tdh.formal.st.identitySums.plain: An identity’s balance, raw and base are the sums of its wallets’.
network.tdh.formal.st.identitySums.scope: The model computes them that way and the vectors check it, but it is not a theorem.
network.tdh.formal.st.minted.title: Held = minted − burned
network.tdh.formal.st.minted.plain: False. A transfer from 0x…dead credits its recipient with a fresh copy and is not a mint. Case G: one copy minted, one sent by 0x…dead, two held. What holds instead is the conservation law above.
network.tdh.formal.st.minted.scope: Proved false with a counterexample the build checks.
network.tdh.formal.st.walletSum.title: Total = sum of wallets
network.tdh.formal.st.walletSum.plain: False. Each record’s boost is computed on its own holdings. Case F: two wallets of one identity each hold one Gradient for 100 days; each wallet record has boost 1.02 and final 102, and the identity has boost 1.04 and final 208. The total is 208, not 204.
network.tdh.formal.st.walletSum.scope: A page that adds up wallet values will not match the total.
network.tdh.formal.st.firstRule.title: The first netting rule
network.tdh.formal.st.firstRule.plain: False: under D131’s first rule, steps inside a transaction could change TDH. Five cases are proved in the kernel; the uniform rule P26 adopted the same day gives equal results in each.
network.tdh.formal.st.firstRule.scope: Totals from the model, first rule against the current one.
network.tdh.formal.st.cap.title: The 19.99% cap
network.tdh.formal.st.cap.plain: With at least six parties, no party, capped or not, counts more than 19.99% of the validators’ weight, and every key’s slice adds up exactly.
network.tdh.formal.st.cap.scope: A separate small model of the cap; group membership and key validity are inputs.
network.tdh.formal.st.exclusions.title: Exclusions
network.tdh.formal.st.exclusions.plain: No evidence shortens an exclusion in force, and exclusions never overlap, stretch or repeat. The proofs also found that recomputing incidents after pruning old evidence could end an exclusion early.
network.tdh.formal.st.exclusions.scope: A finding for the validator specification: fix an incident’s step on the ladder when it opens.
network.tdh.formal.cases.caption: The first netting rule against the current one
network.tdh.formal.cases.desc.A: The order of a pass-through’s two outgoing legs
network.tdh.formal.cases.desc.B: The order of a burn and a forwarded mint
network.tdh.formal.cases.desc.C: Two sends, without and with a round trip appended
network.tdh.formal.cases.desc.D: A round trip placed before a pass-through
network.tdh.formal.cases.desc.E: A mint and a burn inside a pass-through
network.tdh.formal.not.title: What the proofs do not guarantee
network.tdh.formal.not.english.title: That the English text says the same thing.
network.tdh.formal.not.english.body: People check that the model matches the specification; a disagreement is fixed in one or the other and recorded. The model’s authors list ten open questions where P26 leaves a choice.
network.tdh.formal.not.programs.title: That the Rust and Python programs match the model on every input.
network.tdh.formal.not.programs.body: The model and the programs pass the same 51 vectors, and the model matched the Python reference on a whole real day and on 1,000 random inputs, but no machine-checked proof links the programs’ code to the model.
network.tdh.formal.not.inputs.title: That the inputs are right.
network.tdh.formal.not.inputs.body: Selecting and decoding Ethereum logs, state reads and finality are outside the model. Validators are to check every block’s events against Ethereum’s block headers (D118), and two separately written programs are being built to prove each day’s result from Ethereum’s history (D119).
network.tdh.formal.not.rule.title: That the rule is the right rule.
network.tdh.formal.not.rule.body: A proof shows the rule does what it says, not that it is fair or wise. Rule changes are owner decisions.
network.tdh.formal.not.lean.title: Lean itself.
network.tdh.formal.not.lean.body: The proofs rely on Lean’s small kernel and its three standard axioms, which the build audits for every theorem. The 16 numeric checks are evaluations that also trust Lean’s compiler.
network.tdh.formal.layers.title: Three layers of assurance
network.tdh.formal.layers.desc: The English specification is checked against the Lean model by people. Inside the Lean model, the proofs are the only machine-checked links. The model and the programs, the Rust core, program B and the Python reference, pass the same 51 vectors, and the model was compared with the Python reference on a whole day and on 1,000 random inputs. The programs check each other: Rust and Python in the daily comparison, Rust and program B in every validator. Inputs are checked separately.
network.tdh.formal.layers.programsSub: Rust core, program B, Python reference
network.tdh.formal.layers.vectors: 51 shared vectors; a whole day and 1,000 random inputs against Python
network.tdh.formal.layers.inputsBody: Checked reads (D118) and proofs A and B (D119), outside the model
network.tdh.formal.layers.machine: Machine-checked: the proofs inside the Lean model
network.tdh.formal.layers.human: Checked by people or by tests
network.tdh.formal.check.title: How you will be able to check
network.tdh.formal.check.body: The model lives in 6529’s design repository, beside the specification and its vectors. Once that source is published, anyone with Lean installed can rebuild it, which re-checks every proof and audits its axioms, and run the vectors through it:
network.tdh.formal.check.commands:
lake build
lake exe tdh-vectors ../tdh-reference/vectors   # 51 of 51, 976 checks
